description_full: Civeo Corporation engages in hospitality services to the natural resource industry in Canada, Australia, and internationally. The company develops lodges and villages; and mobile assets, including modular, skid-mounted accommodation, and central facilities that provide short to medium-term accommodation needs. It also offers food, housekeeping, and maintenance services, as well as laundry, facility management and maintenance, water and wastewater treatment, power generation, communication system, security, logistics, and camp management services. In addition, the company provides development activities for workforce accommodation facilities, including site selection, permitting, engineering and design, and manufacturing and site construction services, as well as lodging and catering, and hospitality services. It serves oil, mining, engineering, and oilfield and mining service companies. Civeo Corporation was founded in 1977 and is headquartered in Houston, Texas.

financial_summary: Civeo Corporation (Canada) is a small-cap consumer cyclical business with a $369M market cap on $639M of annual revenue.
The top line has compounded at -3% over the past three years and +2% annually across the full decade, and a shrinking top line is the hardest headwind any business can overcome.

Returns on capital run at 1% against a 8% cost of capital, which means the business is destroying value with every dollar it reinvests, and 23% gross margins are typical of commodity economics where competitors can replicate the product cheaply.
The business throws off $2M in free cash flow — roughly 0 cents on every revenue dollar, which is the owner-earnings figure that actually belongs to shareholders.
On the balance sheet, debt is moderate at 2.2× net debt/EBITDA, serviceable in normal conditions but worth watching through a downturn, and thin 0.4× interest coverage leaves no room for a bad year.

Management returns a meaningful 15.5% of market cap to owners through dividends and buybacks, a strong signal of disciplined capital allocation, and insiders hold 7.0% of the shares, and profit capture is only 0.1× the fair share, suggesting no structural edge inside its industry.
